technical_and_design_decisions: Treat s-c-d as Spring Cloud Data Flow, s-c-s as Spring Cloud Skipper, and s-c-s-m as Spring Cloud Stream Modules based on the naming convention used in the user stories.
Use Apache Maven (consistent with the broader Spring Cloud ecosystem) for module/project structure; new modules are added as sub-modules of the existing parent POMs.

Design ModuleRegistry as a Spring-idiomatic service interface with a default in-memory implementation; a file/JSON-backed implementation is used so registration state can be persisted and inspected by the CLI (U7, U8).

The offline mode for AetherModuleResolver is implemented as a strategy/strategy chain pattern so the resolver can fall back from remote Maven resolution to a local file-system based repository without changing the public API of the resolver (U6).
Uber-jar enforcement (U1) is implemented via the Maven Shade Plugin's dependency rules to reject duplicate classes/resources from external libraries rather than overwriting them.
The SFTP port (U3) re-uses the existing Spring Integration sftp support rather than re-implementing the protocol; only the XD-specific module adapter layer is ported.
Processor OOTB modules (U5) are packaged as Maven modules under a dedicated s-c-s-m 'processor' subdirectory following the existing source/sink module conventions.
RedisRule contract tests (U4) are moved to a dedicated test-fixtures module (e.g., s-c-d-redis-rule-tests) consumed by both s-c-d and SI commons, leveraging Maven test-jar packaging.
External library extraction (U2) is a pure refactor: move source, update imports, fix build, no behavioral change.
CLI commands (U8) are implemented on top of the existing Spring Cloud Skipper/Data Flow shell command infrastructure (Spring Shell-based).
assumptions: A single experienced Spring/Java developer performs the work, so estimates exclude onboarding and ramp-up time.
All target repositories already exist locally with build infrastructure in place; no green-field repo setup is required.
No requirement gathering or stakeholder meetings are required - the user stories in the specification are treated as final and complete.
Existing tests in s-c-d, s-c-s, and s-c-s-m are assumed green at the start; refactor/port activities only add or move tests, they do not fix pre-existing test debt.
Unit, integration, and end-to-end test execution time is included within each activity's estimate (not as a separate 'execute tests' activity).
Effort is expressed in productive work-hours of focused development; meetings, code review wait time, and CI queue time are excluded.
Reasonable code review iterations (1-2 rounds per activity) are included in the per-activity estimates.
SFTP module porting from Spring XD assumes the XD code is well understood and documented; the developer does not need to reverse-engineer the original XD module behavior.
Documentation is limited to inline Javadoc, a short README per new module, and updates to existing reference docs - no new user-facing guides or tutorials are produced.
Localization, internationalization, and accessibility concerns are out of scope.

activities.activity_description: Identify the XD SFTP source module, port its configuration metadata and integration code to a Spring Cloud Stream source module in s-c-s, replace XD-specific APIs (e.g., XD module options) with s-c-s module options, add the new module to the module metadata, and verify it builds and registers correctly.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Create isolated project for @RedisRule contract tests
activities.activity_description: Create a new Maven module (test-jar packaging) that owns all @RedisRule-related JUnit/TestNG contract tests. Move existing rule tests out of core s-c-d code into the new module, wire it as a test dependency in s-c-d and in SI commons (or equivalent), and ensure the rule still applies to all targeted test classes.

Create a new Maven project (s-c-s-m processor base) that defines the processor module conventions, a processor base class, common option metadata, and a sample 'transform' or 'filter' processor module so developers can build streaming pipelines from s-c-s-m processors.

Add an 'offline' configuration flag to AetherModuleResolver, implement a local-file-system based artifact resolution strategy (no remote Maven calls), wire it through the resolver's strategy chain, add unit and integration tests covering local resolution, and update configuration documentation.

Define the ModuleRegistry SPI (register, unregister, lookup-by-name, list), provide a default file/JSON-backed implementation that can be enabled in s-c-d and s-c-s, expose it as a Spring bean, and add unit tests plus an integration test that exercises the full lookup lifecycle.

activities.activity_name: U8 - module info / list / register / unregister CLI commands
activities.activity_description: Implement the four shell commands on top of Spring Shell, delegating to the ModuleRegistry service. Cover input validation, helpful error messages, and a 'list' output that is both human-readable and script-friendly (e.g., name + coordinates). Add command-level tests.

Run a full end-to-end test pass: build all affected modules, run the existing s-c-d and s-c-s test suites plus the new U3/U5/U6/U7/U8 tests, fix any regressions introduced by the new modules or the U2 refactor, and verify the uber-jar produced after U1 still has the expected (non-overridden) contents.

Update READMEs and reference docs for the new modules (U2, U4, U5, U7), document the new CLI commands (U8), document the offline mode flag (U6) and the SFTP source module usage (U3), and add a short note about the shade-plugin override behavior change (U1).
